subject: Systematic bias due to instrument sensitivity drop-off

messages.author: c483b92662bdebf1
messages.subject: Systematic bias due to instrument sensitivity drop-off
parts:
Hi MSstats group,

Thank you for your continued support.

I have performed a targeted analysis from two mouse tissues (10-biological replicates, paired design with heavy labeled reference standards).
One tissue type was run in January, and the second several months later in April. During this period there was a substantial drop-off in instrument sensitivity (see pic).

I'd like to analyze for differentially expressed proteins (Tissue 1. v Tissue 2.)
I believe MSstats' "Equalize medians" normalization will account for this bias, but I wanted to ask to make sure.

Thanks,
Tyler

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Systematic bias due to instrument sensitivity drop-off
parts:
Dear Tyler,

This experiment is a non-starter from a statistical viewpoint. Since the tissue acquisitions were not randomized, you have a confounding between the tissue type and the date of data acquisition. No amount of normalization will be able to fully correct for that. This dataset in unlikely to yield any sound result. Our best advice is to start over, with an appropriate experimental design.

There are numerous examples of research that is irreproducible, due to lack of randomization. See, e.g., here  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15814023

Sincerely
OV
